reviews.review:
Progression in UnderMine 2 is heavily constrained by its key economy. Each floor effectively requires at least three keys: one for the shop, one for the altar room, and one for the relic room. From the third or fourth floor onward, the game becomes noticeably stingier with key drops, instead flooding runs with bombs or no pickups at all for no reasons. As a result, it becomes practically impossible to access everything a floor offers in later stages. In reality, the required number of keys is even higher, often between five and ten, since many puzzles and optional rewards also consume keys, making an already scarce resource feel artificially rare.

In terms of content, a substantial portion of the relics and bosses are carried over directly from UnderMine. Rather than feeling like a true successor, the game comes across as an overpriced DLC. In fact, it feels as though more features from the first game have been removed than genuinely new content has been added.

Notably absent are systems such as pet leveling and the sack that allowed players to retain a portion of their gold after death. While this might seem nitpicky for an early access title, these mechanics already existed in the first game, which raises the question of why they are missing here at all. The current development approach gives the impression that content from UnderMine 1 is simply being reintroduced gradually into UnderMine 2, primarily to make it compatible with co-op, a mode that is neither online nor particularly accessible, as it is limited to split-screen play. Appeals to remote play are not especially convincing either, as not every player has a good enough internet connection to make that a viable option.

Ultimately, this is still more UnderMine. UnderMine is a good game, and for that reason alone there is enjoyment to be found here. Nevertheless, UnderMine 2 feels uncomfortably close to a lazy cash grab. 

A cautious approach is strongly recommended: waiting for the full release before deciding whether the amount of new content justifies the steep price seems sensible. Until then, returning to UnderMine 1 is arguably the better option, as the differences are barely noticeable.
